chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir.

He said: Awn ibn Abdullah ibn Masud became ill, so I went to visit him (in his illness). He said: Shall I not narrate a hadith from Abdullah ibn Masud to you? I said: Yes, of course. He said: Abdullah said:

While we were with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), he suddenly smiled. So I said: What is the matter with you, O Messenger of God — why did you smile? He said: I am astonished at the believer and his fear of illness. If he only knew what reward he receives through illness, he would love to remain ill until he meets his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.الثواب: Reward, spiritual merit — the divine compensation for patient endurance of suffering
key_terms.السقم: Illness, sickness — the means through which divine reward is accrued
key_terms.جزع: Anxiety, fear, anguish — used for the believer's negative reaction to illness
key_terms.عز وجل: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific formula for God

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the reward for illness in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain from Ibn Masud, records the Prophet smiling to himself before revealing a profound insight: a believer's fear of illness reveals a lack of awareness of its spiritual reward. The Prophet taught that if believers truly understood the spiritual merit accrued through patient endurance of illness, they would not dread it — indeed, they would welcome the continuation of illness as a path to drawing closer to God. This reflects the broader Islamic teaching that trials and suffering, endured with patience and faith, carry immense divine reward and purification.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from `Abdullah b. Sinan from Muhammad b. al-Munkadir.
He said: `Awn b. Abdullah b. Masud became ill, so I went to visit him, so he said: Shall I not narrate a hadith from `Abdullah b. Mas`ud to you? I said: Of course. He said: `Abdullah said:

We were with the Messenger of Allah (s) [one day] when he smiled. So, I said: Why do you smile, O Messenger of Allah? He said: I am astonished at the believer and his fear of illness. If he knew of the good deeds he reaped from illness, he would want to continue being ill until he meets his Lord.
